intro: Voice removes friction so honest logging happens. Speak the meal, review the transcript and estimate, then save — especially powerful when your hands are full.
buddyTip: Say the protein first, then sides, then oils and drinks: “chicken, rice, broccoli, olive oil, sparkling water.”
mission: Log your next meal with voice from Home and confirm before save.
why: Typing every ingredient fails on busy days. Voice keeps capture close to the plate, which improves honesty versus midnight reconstruction.
Spoken logs also encourage completeness: when you talk, you remember sauces and the second bread roll more often than when you tap three generic items.
Voice is not magic — accents, noise, and vague phrases need your confirmation. The confirm step is the coaching moment, not a nuisance.

points: Start from Home mic / Talk food
Speak clearly; include oils, drinks, and approximate portions
Adjust before save when something is wrong
Find the meal afterward in Foodiary for fine edits

misconceptions.myth: If the transcript isn’t perfect, the log is useless.
misconceptions.truth: Fix key foods and portions on confirm. Directional honesty beats silence.

misconceptions.myth: Voice means I shouldn’t use camera or text.
misconceptions.truth: Mix modes. Voice for speed; camera for complex plates; text for labels.

steps: List foods with rough amounts (“two eggs,” “a fist of rice,” “a teaspoon oil”)
Mention cooking method if it changes fat (“fried,” “grilled,” “with cream sauce”)
Pause; review what Buddy heard and estimated
Confirm save; skim Foodiary later only if needed
how.buddyHelps: Buddy turns speech into structured diary entries with estimates. Confirmation keeps you in control while still moving fast.

sections.title: Noisy environments
paras: Cup a hand, face away from the room, or step aside. If recognition fails twice, switch to photo or text — don’t abandon the log.

sections.title: Privacy
paras: Be mindful in quiet offices or shared spaces. Short phrases work; you don’t need to narrate your life story.

mistakes.quote: I said “lunch” and expected Buddy to invent the plate.
mistakes.why: Voice needs content. Name foods and portions.

mistakes.quote: I saved without reading the estimate and got angry later.
mistakes.why: Confirm is part of the flow. Ten seconds prevents bad ledger rows.

mistakes.quote: Mic failed once so I stopped logging for the day.
mistakes.why: Switch input mode. The meal still deserves a diary line.

encouragement: Talk food like you’re telling a friend what you ate. Buddy listens, estimates, and keeps the day honest — you stay in charge at confirm.
